issues.body: Section 4 says a point-in-time GraphQL queue/arm read is the right guard because it licenses an action taken “now,” and presents `not-queued and not-armed -> draft it` as fail-closed. But `review_state()` and the later draft-conversion API call are separate requests with no head binding or compare-and-swap. A PR can become queued, armed, or review-passed after the probe and before conversion; the conversion can then evict or un-arm exactly the live merge the guard is meant to protect. Reusing `backfill-provenance.review_state` preserves that TOCTOU window rather than resolving it. This also undercuts the claim that all listed failure directions are closed.
issues.fix_hint: Revise the recommendation to specify and justify a race-safe mutation protocol. For example, establish a GitHub-supported conditional/atomic operation, or add a post-mutation detection-and-recovery protocol whose safety is demonstrated; if neither is possible, explicitly reject automatic draft conversion or require human execution. Add the queue/arm transition between probe and mutation as a mandatory adversarial test/design case.
issues.title: Draft-conversion recommendation has an unaddressed probe-to-mutation race

verdict.summary: The record correctly rejects a point-in-time queue absence as durable evidence for freeing a crate, but then relies on the same point-in-time evidence to authorize a separate draft mutation without addressing the race between the GraphQL read and that mutation. That leaves the recommended remedy capable of evicting a PR that becomes queued or armed after the probe. Because this is the load-bearing safety claim of the proposed follow-up, the design is not yet sound enough to approve.
